facts.sequence_limit: Endpoints only. No intermediate swap timing, causal sequence, or survival at the enemy death is inferred by this computation.

facts.resource_count_limit: Exact source-listed labels, deduplicated within each match. They include uncertain or offensive entries and are not verified forced-resource frequencies.
facts.cc_count_limit: Literal mentions in observed notes, including negated/uncertain/post-death mentions. These are search aids, not counts of landed CC.
facts.recovery_count_limit: Field coverage only: texts may explicitly say no reset. Not a reset-event rate.

hypotheses.statement: One opening target also explains every reported enemy kill in wins.

hypotheses.statement: Warlock is vulnerable to renewed pressure while healing and pet interference are sufficiently constrained; permanent pet removal is not an established prerequisite.
hypotheses.limitation: Pet work is not sufficient, and kills occur with a pet still present or Paladin free late. The three Paladin kills differ: only one explicitly shows severe mana depletion.

opening_target.text: Destruction Warlock; recorded in 13/16 games. This is the labeled opening target, not necessarily the first sustained coordinated damage.

initial_objective.text: Develop Warlock pressure while disrupting Paladin healing and Succubus interference.

win_condition.text: Warlock is vulnerable to renewed pressure while healing and pet interference are sufficiently constrained; permanent pet removal is not an established prerequisite.

manufacture.text: Usually open Warlock. Repeated pet pressure and Seduction/summon interruptions occur between player attempts; return to meaningful player damage with healer disruption.

conversion.text: Usually commit Warlock. Later Paladin branches also convert when Warlock control and real healer damage align.

reset.text: After player or pet recovery, renew disruption and return to a fresh player-pressure window; replacement summons mean pet absence cannot be assumed to persist.

assessment.text: Repeated support-interference problem. Pressure and interruptions are observed; pet death and permanent removal are often unconfirmed.
